primitives.name: DeepHit Survival Forecasting
primitives.verbatim_quote: This study investigates the feasibility of using a DeepHit neural network to forecast time-to-injury from longitudinal athlete monitoring data, while providing interpretable predictions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S(t | x)': 'Survival probability at time t given covariates x', 'H(τ | x)': 'Base hazard function at event time τ given covariates x'}
primitives.assumptions: Longitudinal athlete monitoring data assumed complete and error-free; proportional hazards assumption relaxed via neural network flexibility.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High-dimensional covariate space with sparse event times leads to overfitting without proper regularization.

layer2.mapping: GSI Mapping: DeepHit serves as a conformal survival ensemble, producing probabilistic injury forecasts that calibrate against empirical league injury rates.
layer2.telemetry: Calibration error on holdout test sets measures forecast reliability.

primitives.name: Shapley Additive Explanations
primitives.verbatim_quote: Overall, this study provides a novel proof of concept: survival modelling with DeepHit shows strong potential to advance injury forecasting in football, offering accurate, explainable, and actionable insights for injury prevention across competitive levels.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\phi_i': 'Marginal contribution of feature i to the prediction f', 'S': 'Subset of features excluding i', 'N': 'Full set of features', 'n': 'Total number of features'}
primitives.assumptions: Feature independence within coalitions is assumed, though interaction terms can be incorporated via extended SHAP formulations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-linear interactions between covariates cause feature importance to shift, necessitating cooperative game theory for stable attribution.

layer2.mapping: GSI Mapping: SHAP values provide local variable importance scores for Bayesian model calibration, informing posterior shrinkage priors on key risk factors.
layer2.telemetry: SHAP summary plots reveal dominant drivers of injury risk in real-time.

primitives.name: Chronological Validation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Baseline models (Random Forest, XGBoost, Logistic Regression) were optimised via grid search for benchmarking, while the DeepHit model, implemented with a multilayer perceptron backbone, was evaluated using chronological and leave-one-player-out (LOPO) validation.
primitives.assumptions: Temporal ordering preserved; future data not leaked into training set.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Season-to-season variations introduce distributional shifts that degrade out-of-sample performance.

layer2.mapping: GSE Mapping: Chronological validation implements a sliding window state-transition framework, updating player states based on sequential telemetry.
layer2.telemetry: Validation loss on recent data tracks player-specific injury risk dynamics.

primitives.name: Concordance Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: DeepHit achieved a concordance index of 0.762, outperforming baseline models and delivering individualised, time-varying risk estimates.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C-index': 'Discrimination metric ranging from 0.5 (random) to 1.0 (perfect)', 'concordant pairs': 'Pairs of observations where higher predicted risk corresponds to earlier event time'}
primitives.assumptions: Independence of event times; censored observations properly accounted for via inverse probability weighting.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Imbalanced event ratios inflate variance; rare injuries reduce statistical power to distinguish models.

layer2.mapping: GSI Mapping: C-index maps to Bayes factor under proportional hazards, enabling hypothesis testing on model superiority.
layer2.telemetry: Track C-index trends to assess incremental value of new telemetry modalities.

reasoning_traces.think:
DeepHit integrates multi-layer perceptrons with mixture-of-competitors objectives, decomposing survival functions into component risks. Its core failure mode is overfitting on high-dimensional monitoring data; regularization via dropout and early stopping mitigates this. In contrast, traditional Cox models assume linearity in log-hazard, which we relax by learning non-linear mappings from longitudinal covariates to time-to-event distributions. The Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) provide game-theoretic attribution of risk contributions, addressing model interpretability concerns raised by 'black box' deep learning. Chronological validation ensures temporal causality, preventing information leakage from future events. The concordance index evaluates discriminatory power, accounting for censoring via inverse probability weighting. Together, these primitives form a robust pipeline for actionable injury forecasting.
